stories.title: Instant Reaction: US Adds 165,000 Jobs, Topping All Forecasts
stories.take: 165,000 jobs added in October, more than double the 70,000 forecast, with upward revisions taking the combined figure to 249,000 • Unemployment slipped to 4.1% and participation rose to 61.9%, but underemployment rose to 7.9% • Claudia Sahm: low-hire, low-fire endures — the beat is welcome, but job-seekers still struggle and she needs several months to call it a real acceleration

stories.title: Pete Hegseth under pressure after US elections
stories.take: Democrats taking Congress are expected to target Hegseth with impeachment hearings on the Iran war, alleged drug-smuggler killings, and the Maduro seizure • Rep. Thomas Massie says he will file articles next week; Hegseth calls it a sham and Trump backs him — but a replacement is easier to confirm before the Senate flips • Tech shares plunged Thursday on AI-regulation fears, with the Nasdaq in correction and chip stocks in a bear market

stories.title: Tech stocks tank over AI panic
stories.take: Nasdaq lost an estimated $2.5 trillion in a day; Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's Kospi both closed down 6% • BBC's read: the midterms sparked it, but the deeper doubt is whether $1.8 trillion committed to AI ever pays — Samsung and SK Hynix are about half of Korea's whole market • Also: Kenya's doomsday cult leader sentenced to 200 years, Paraguay's president faces impeachment after a bank collapse froze half the country's accounts, and Newsom's death-row commutations drew a promise of a court challenge

stories.title: Why the Tech Right Lost Big This Week
stories.take: The answer, per Ezra Klein: the tech right attached itself to Trump and gave him his unpopular pro-AI, pro-data-center stance — 56% of voters called AI and data centers a major factor, and 76% opposed a data center in their community • Musk spent about $470–500 million and got almost nothing; his spending became the closing attack theme in races like Paxton's in Texas • The diagnosis: the tech right tried to ram AI through without convincing anyone to want it, and money loses when the candidates and politics are bad

stories.title: The Macro Implications of the Blue Tsunami
stories.take: Democrats took the House and Senate with swings up to 20 points from 2024 in some counties — a structural win that shapes the Supreme Court and the Fed for years • Texas flipped hard blue in statewide races, while California's billionaire tax failed and Prop 42's ban on new personal-property taxes won big • Gridlock is not total, but tariff relief would require peeling off farm-state Republicans — a tail scenario, per Employ America's Skanda Amarnath

stories.title: How to Reset the Course of a Nation, with Rachel Maddow
stories.take: Maddow's answer: reset through accountability — congressional oversight and impeachments (she names Todd Blanche, citing pardon-for-donor cases), and bar corrupt officials from public service for life • Rebuild a Department of Justice she calls effectively dead, and return to policy that lowers costs: health insurance, student-loan relief, help for farmers hit by trade policy • Refuse the scapegoat frame, point and laugh at ham-handed attacks, link corruption to affordability — 'they are robbing you blind and that is why you are poor' — and keep turnout up

stories.title: Is This The End Of MAGA? — ft. Anthony Scaramucci
stories.take: Scaramucci's answer: yes, as it was — a total repudiation and full-on blowout — but no non-MAGA successor is ready; 'not the beginning of the end, but the end of the beginning' • He says with confidence the 2028 GOP frontrunner will NOT be JD Vance or Marco Rubio, both too Trump-dipped to escape the loss • Markets are bullish on gridlock — split government has historically favored stocks and bonds — with AI and data centers flagged as the concrete ballot-box risk

stories.title: Chuck Schumer on Governing With (Or Without) Trump
stories.take: Schumer, poised to become Senate Majority Leader again, credits the 'three Cs' — costs, corruption, chaos — and candidates recruited to fit red and purple states • Recruitment examples: Mary Peltola in Alaska, Sherrod Brown in Ohio (Schumer flew to Columbus three times), and Scott Colom in Mississippi, leading by about 1,700 votes • On whether Democrats won or Trump lost, Schumer says all three: bad Trump record, issue focus, and good candidates

stories.title: Caution: Men NOT at Work
stories.take: October added 165,000 jobs and unemployment fell to 4.1%, but women now hold more US jobs than men — only the third time that has ever happened • Young men's labor-force participation is down 13% since 2000, the steepest drop of any age group, after manufacturing's decline, opioids, and the Great Recession's construction hit • The proposed fix: apprenticeships, community college and trades over college-only paths, plus pushing men toward care jobs — nurse practitioners pay about $132,000 median with 40%-plus demand growth, yet only about 10% of nurses are men

stories.title: Raman celebrates victory, LA City Council race separated by 600 votes, Outrage at Newsom over death penalty— Morning Edition
stories.take: Mayor-elect Nithya Raman, LA's first mayor of Asian descent, takes office December 14 after beating Karen Bass, the first incumbent mayor to lose in more than two decades • Council District 3 is separated by fewer than 600 votes and District 9 by about 1,500 • Outrage follows Newsom commuting all California death-row sentences to life without parole; LA and Orange County DAs say they will still consider the death penalty in new cases

stories.title: Big Tech lost big in the 2026 election
stories.take: Corruption polled as voters' number one issue and almost every measure to block data centers passed — the hosts say those are the same vote, against tech buying favors and what the favors were for • Musk's roughly $500 million bought nothing, and Democrats will now come for AI companies; only great products save them, because courts are unlikely to give AI firms the cute-newcomer pass Google got in the 2000s • A reporter 'brightened' a photo in ChatGPT and actually generated a different bag and shoes — the hosts call the confusion 'computational relativism'

stories.title: Post-Election Market & Jobs, Why Gas Prices Could Stay High, Trump's Arch Blocked
stories.take: Why gas prices could stay high: crude is not pump fuel — even if the Iran war ended tomorrow, Hormuz shipping, refinery runs and the whole refined supply chain must recover; optimistic case is crude down $15–20 fast but pump prices taking months, pessimistic case is a year • Jobs beat expectations while September inflation at 3.7% outran 3% wage growth, and stocks erased their post-election gains in a sell-off of at least 3% across the major indexes • A federal judge blocked construction of Trump's 250-foot arch for 14 days, hours after the planning commission approved it

stories.title: Instagram Wants to be YouTube Now?
stories.take: Yes — Instagram is launching long-form horizontal video with a new tab, widescreen videos at the top of Explore, and TV apps including a new Apple TV app • Reels that are clips can now link to the full long-form video — the YouTube funnel — so Instagram keeps viewers instead of losing them to wherever the full video lives • No YouTube-style revenue share was announced, only a selective bonus program, and the hosts split on whether it works without paying creators consistently

stories.title: Is Anthropic’s $1.5 Trillion Valuation Too Rich?
stories.take: Yes — investors set to back the IPO told the Journal $1.5 trillion is no longer achievable in the AI sell-off; one put a realistic valuation closer to $1 trillion, another raised delaying the listing • Anthropic must decide within days — roadshow was due next week, IPO planned before Thanksgiving — whether to proceed for less, shrink the offering to defend valuation, or delay; its revenue run rate topped $80 billion at the end of October • The sell-off is global: Japan's Nikkei is in bear-market territory and South Korea's main index is down 44% since its June peak
